title: kith-core: Contact data type
description:
What: Define Contact struct in src/contact.rs.

Module file: crates/kith-core/src/contact.rs — create this file, then add 'pub mod contact;' to src/lib.rs.

Algorithm:
1. Define Contact struct:
   id: String
   tailscale_user_id: String  → #[serde(rename="tailscaleUserId")]
   login: String
   mailbox_host: String  → #[serde(rename="mailboxHost")]
   display_name: Option<String>  → #[serde(rename="displayName", skip_serializing_if="Option::is_none")]
   first_seen_at: String  → #[serde(rename="firstSeenAt")]  (UTCDate)
   last_seen_at: String  → #[serde(rename="lastSeenAt")]  (UTCDate)
   blocked: bool
   Derives: Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize.
2. Add a comment on tailscale_user_id: '// Opaque stable key. Never parse or assume format.'
3. Add display_name helper: impl Contact { pub fn display_name_or_fallback(&self) -> &str { ... } }
   Returns: display_name if Some and non-empty, else login if non-empty, else tailscale_user_id.
4. Add 'pub mod contact;' to src/lib.rs.
5. Run: cargo check -p kith-core

Defensive programming rules:
- tailscale_user_id is opaque — no methods that parse it as email or structured data
- display_name_or_fallback must never return empty string
- No unwrap() in helper methods

Tests (independent oracle: manually constructed JSON matching JMAP field names):
- Round-trip: construct Contact, serialize to JSON, deserialize, assert equality
- JSON field names: assert serialized JSON uses "tailscaleUserId", "mailboxHost", "firstSeenAt", "lastSeenAt"
- display_name_or_fallback: test all three fallback cases
- blocked=false: assert serializes as JSON false (not 0 or null)
